title: Golden example — a three scene walkthrough

scenes.title: One question, one clock
scenes.mermaid:
flowchart LR
    Q["A question"] --> A["Evidence"] --> D["A decision"]
    style Q fill:#fff4e5,stroke:#e8a33d
    style D fill:#e8f6ec,stroke:#3d9a5b
captions: Three scenes is enough to show the shape.
Everything you see is positioned on one clock, and that clock is measured, not guessed.
scenes.narration: Three scenes is enough to show the shape. Everything you see is positioned on one clock, and that clock is measured, not guessed.

scenes.title: The clock is derived from the audio
scenes.mermaid:
flowchart TB
    C["Clip lengths"] --> S["Scene starts"]
    S --> P["Playback position"]
    P --> V["Visuals and captions"]
    style C fill:#eef4ff,stroke:#5b8def
    style V fill:#e8f6ec,stroke:#3d9a5b
captions: Each clip is measured, then the scene starts are summed from those measurements.
So a clip always fills its slot exactly, and jumping anywhere lands in the right place.
scenes.narration: Each clip is measured, then the scene starts are summed from those measurements. So a clip always fills its slot exactly, and jumping anywhere lands in the right place.

scenes.title: It ends by asking
scenes.mermaid:
flowchart TD
    Q["What next?"] --> A["Keep it"]
    Q --> B["Change it"]
    Q --> C["Park it"]
    style Q fill:#eef4ff,stroke:#5b8def
    style A fill:#e8f6ec,stroke:#3d9a5b
    style C fill:#f4f4f4,stroke:#bbb
captions: When something is still open, the walkthrough says so and asks.
Tell me which of the three you want, in the chat. Type it, or use the microphone.
scenes.narration: When something is still open, the walkthrough says so and asks. Tell me which of the three you want, in the chat. Type it, or use the microphone.

disposition.prompt: What should happen to this example?
disposition.note: Any answer works, including none. Type it in the chat, or use the microphone.
